concerns.text: T014a (Generate Stopwords) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T013 (Orchestrator) to provide data for analysis. A task cannot be parallel-safe if it requires the output of a preceding sequential task. The [P] tag is incorrect here.

T014 (Tokenizer) depends on T014a (Stopword Generator), but T014a is marked [P]. If T014a is truly parallel-safe, it implies it has no dependencies, yet the description says 'Depends on T013'. This creates a logical contradiction in the dependency graph: T014a cannot be both a parallel task and a dependent task in the same phase block without explicit ordering.

T023 (Aligner) depends on T020 (Fitter) across all 5 windows. T020 is marked [P], implying it can run in parallel. However, T023 cannot start until *all* instances of T020 are complete. The current ordering implies T023 might start after just one T020 instance if the [P] tag is interpreted as 'start immediately'. The dependency chain needs explicit 'Wait for all T020' semantics.

T029 (Permutation) depends on T029a (Stratified Sampling), T020 (Fitter), and T023 (Aligner). T029a is marked [P] but depends on T016/T016a. T029 is not marked [P] (correct), but the dependency on T029a (which is marked [P]) creates a risk of T029 starting before T029a finishes if the scheduler treats [P] as 'no dependencies'. The [P] tag on T029a is misleading given its explicit dependencies.

T016a (Partition Validator) is listed after T016 (Saver) and marked as depending on it. However, T016a is not marked [P], which is correct. The text 'Depends on T016' is clear, but the visual grouping in Phase 3 mixes [P] and non-[P] tasks without clear visual separation of the dependency chain, potentially confusing the execution order.
